info.title: AerScheduler API
info.summary: Schedule aircraft, close out flights, and bill for them — from your own software.
info.description:
The AerScheduler REST API. Everything the mobile app and the web console can do, your own software can do too — schedule aircraft, close flights out, invoice them, and pull the numbers back.

This is the same API our own clients use. There is no separate "public" tier and no second implementation to fall behind.

## Getting started

```bash
# 1. Sign in. The token is good for 30 days.
curl -s -X POST https://api.aerscheduler.com/auth \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"you@yourschool.com","password":"…"}'

# 2. Use it.
curl -s https://api.aerscheduler.com/resources/planes \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

## Conventions

Every one of these holds across the whole API, so you can write one client wrapper and stop thinking about it:

- **Responses are wrapped.** A body-bearing success is `{ "data": … }`. An error is `{ "message": "…" }`, and the message is written to be safe to show a user. A few endpoints noted individually break this: `/health`, the CSV export, and the OAuth redirects.
- **Status codes mean what they say.** `200` read or update, `201` created, `204` done with nothing to return, `400` your request was wrong, `401` sign in again, `403` signed in but not allowed, `404` no such thing, `429` slow down.
- **`401` and `403` are different.** `401` means the token is dead — get a new one. `403` means the token is fine and the answer is still no; retrying will not help.
- **Collections are `GET /thing`, items are `GET /thing/{id}`.** Create is `POST` to the collection, update is `PATCH` to the item, delete is `DELETE` on the item. Where a resource deviates, the endpoint says so.
- **Your organization is implied.** The token carries it. You never pass an organization id, and you can never read another organization's records.
- **Ids are integers** and stable for the life of the record.
- **Money is in cents**, as an integer. Never a float.

## Time zones

Scheduling is anchored to the **airport's** time zone, not the caller's device. A booking made at 7am at the field is 7am at the field regardless of where the person making it happens to be.

In practice that means: send `start` and `end` with an **explicit UTC offset or `Z`**. A bare local datetime like `2026-08-04T15:00:00` is rejected — it would be read in the server's zone and silently book a different instant than the person picked. Send `timeZoneName` (an IANA zone) alongside so the booking knows which zone it was made in.

## Reservation types

Which `type` a caller may create depends on the roles they hold. Roles are additive: an instructor who is also a technician may create both sets.

| Role | May create |
|---|---|
| owner, admin, dispatcher | solo, dual, ground, guest, sim, rental, maintenance |
| instructor | solo, dual, ground, guest, sim |
| student | solo, dual, ground, sim |
| renter | rental |
| technician | maintenance |

## Rate limits

Limits are applied per signed-in account, not per IP, so a whole school behind one office address does not share one budget.

| | Limit |
|---|---|
| Per account | 300 requests/minute, 5,000/hour |
| Unauthenticated | 100 requests per 5 minutes, per IP |
| Sign-in and password reset | Tighter still, per IP and per email address |

Every response carries `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining`, and `RateLimit-Reset`. A `429` carries `Retry-After` in seconds — honour it rather than retrying on a fixed interval.

## Pagination

There isn't any yet, and you should know that before you build against a list endpoint. Every collection returns its full set. Date-ranged endpoints (`/reservations`, the reports) are the ones to lean on for large data — `/reservations` requires a window for exactly this reason. Cursor pagination is planned, and will be additive: an unpaginated request will keep returning what it returns today.

## Versioning

This document describes **v1.0.0**. Additive changes — new endpoints, new fields on an existing response — ship without notice, so parse leniently and ignore fields you do not recognise. Anything that would break a working integration gets a new major version and an announcement first.

post.description:
Exchanges an email and password for a bearer token valid for **30 days**. Send that token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every other request.

The token is scoped to one organization — whichever is active for the account. If the account belongs to several, switch with `POST /organizations/switch/{orgId}`, which returns a fresh token scoped to the new one.

post.description:
Books a resource, a person, or both.

`start` and `end` **must carry an explicit UTC offset or `Z`**. A bare local datetime is rejected: it would be read in the server's zone and silently book a different instant than the customer picked.

Which `type` values you may create depends on your roles — see the Reservation types section. The server also refuses double-bookings and bookings on grounded aircraft.

Pass a `recurrence` object to create a repeating series. Occurrences are real reservations, so each one can be ramped, reviewed, and invoiced independently.

201.description: The booking that was created, or the series.

400.description: Rejected: a clash, a grounded aircraft, an ambiguous timestamp, or a type your roles may not create.

401.description: No token, an expired token, or a malformed one. Sign in again.

403.description: Authenticated, but not allowed to do this.

429.description: Rate limited. `Retry-After` says how long to wait.

type.description: What kind of booking. Restricted by the caller's roles — see the table above.

start.description: Start instant. Must carry an explicit offset or `Z`.

end.description: End instant. Must carry an explicit offset or `Z`.

timeZoneName.description: IANA zone the booking is being made in — the field's zone, not the caller's device.

notes.description: Free-text notes shown on the booking.

resource.description: The aircraft, simulator, or room to book, as `{ id }`.

location.description: Where it happens, as `{ id }`. Defaults to the resource's location.

personnel.description: Who is on the booking. One person cannot fill two seats on the same booking.

bearerAuth.description:
A bearer token from `POST /auth`, valid for 30 days. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

The token is scoped to a single organization. To act on another, call `POST /organizations/switch/{orgId}` and use the token it returns.

coordinates.description: Geocoded position, when the address could be resolved.

Organization.description: A flight school, club, or FBO. Every other record belongs to exactly one.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

code.description: Six-character join code members use to request access.

showInDirectory.description: Whether the organization opts into the public directory.

coordinates.description: Geocoded position, when the address could be resolved.

Location.description: A base of operations — a field, hangar, or classroom building.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

showInDirectory.description: Whether this location appears in the public directory.

timeZone.description: IANA time zone of the field, e.g. `America/Denver`. Scheduling is anchored to the AIRPORT's zone, not the caller's device — see the Time zones section.

coordinates.description: Geocoded position, when the address could be resolved.

Plane.description: Aircraft-specific detail on a resource whose type is a plane.

categoryClass.description: One of `single-engine land`, `multi-engine land`, `single-engine sea`, `multi-engine sea`.

rampedIn.description: True when the aircraft is on the ramp and available.

grounded.description: True when the aircraft is unavailable for booking.

fuelEngine2.description: Fuel on board, engine 2, for twins.

dryRate.description: Dry rate per hour, in cents.

wetRate.description: Wet rate per hour, in cents.

Resource.description: Anything that can be booked: an aircraft, a simulator, or a room. The `type` object carries whichever detail applies.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

type.description: Exactly one of these is populated.

User.description: A person. One account can belong to many organizations.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

email.description: Email address. Unique across the system.

emailVerifiedAt.description: When the address was verified. Null means unverified.

OrganizationUser.description: A person's membership of an organization. This — not `User` — is what schedules, invoices, and permissions hang off, because one person can belong to several organizations with different roles in each.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

roles.description: Roles held in this organization. Additive and non-hierarchical: a person can be both instructor and technician.

Reservation.description: A booking of a resource, a person, or both.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

title.description: Short label shown on the calendar.

type.description: What kind of booking this is. Which types a caller may CREATE depends on their roles — see the Reservation types section.

start.description: Start instant. MUST carry an explicit offset or `Z`.

end.description: End instant. MUST carry an explicit offset or `Z`.

timeZoneName.description: IANA zone the booking was made in, e.g. `America/Denver`.

cancelledAt.description: When it was cancelled. Null for a live booking.

cancellationCategory.description: Fixed-list reason. Null on bookings cancelled before this was introduced — reports count those as “Not recorded”, not “Other”.

rrule.description: Recurrence rule, when this booking belongs to a repeating series.

review.description: Close-out figures, populated once the flight is ramped out and back in.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

resolvedAt.description: When it was cleared. Null while open.

MaintenanceReminder.description: A due-date or due-hours reminder against one aircraft.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

startHours.description: Meter reading the interval started at.

completedAt.description: When the work was signed off.

MaintenanceReminderTemplate.description: The rule a maintenance reminder repeats on.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

repeat.description: Whether a new interval starts when this one is signed off.

ground.description: Whether the aircraft is grounded when this comes due.

remindDays.description: Interval in days, for date-based reminders.

remindDaysBefore.description: How many days ahead to warn.

remindHours.description: Interval in hours, for meter-based reminders.

remindHoursBefore.description: How many hours ahead to warn.

Invoice.description: A bill for a completed reservation.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

paidAt.description: When it was paid. Null while outstanding.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

expireAt.description: When it stops being shown. Expired notices are swept hourly.

forRoles.description: Roles that should see it. Empty means everyone.

Notification.description: An in-app notification for one member.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

link.description: Deep link into the app or console.

readAt.description: When it was read. Null while unread.

CurrencyType.description: A recurring requirement members must stay current on — a flight review, a medical, a checkout.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

expiresOn.description: A fixed expiry date, for one-off requirements.

warningPeriodInDays.description: How long before expiry to start warning.

canRenewSelf.description: Whether a member may sign off their own renewal.

instructorCanRenew.description: Whether an instructor may sign it off.

dispatcherCanRenew.description: Whether a dispatcher may sign it off.

Currency.description: One member's standing against one currency type. Created automatically when a type is attached to a member group — there is no endpoint that creates one directly.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

DocumentType.description: A category of member document — medical, photo ID, endorsement.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

restricted.description: When true, only administrators may upload documents of this type on a member's behalf.

UserDocument.description: A file held against a member.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

url.description: Location of the file. Fetch through the signed-URL endpoint rather than linking directly.

Group.description: A named set of members or resources, used to scope requirements and permissions in bulk.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

Availability.description: A window in which a person or resource is free.

ReportResult.description: The output of a report run.

unit.description: Unit, where the value is not a plain number.

rows.description: Result rows, keyed by column key.

totals.description: Column totals, where the column is summable.

SearchResults.description: Matches across every entity type the caller may see.

AuthEnvelope.description: Returned by every endpoint that establishes a session.

auth.description: The credential to send on subsequent requests.

Error.description: Every error response has this shape.

message.description: Human-readable explanation, safe to show a user.

retryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before retrying. Present on 429 only.
